references.text: Rachel steals the family's household gods (teraphim), showing that the family had foreign gods which Jacob would later remove.
Rachel hides the stolen household gods, demonstrating the family's involvement with foreign gods that are later removed in Gen 35:4.
Jacob commands his family to remove foreign gods, cleanse themselves, and change their clothes – this is the direct reason they give up the gods and earrings in verse 4.
The earrings used to make the golden calf show a connection between earrings and idolatry, parallel to the earrings given to Jacob.
Joshua commands the people to remove foreign gods from among them and turn their hearts to the Lord, paralleling Jacob's cleansing.
The people remove foreign gods and serve the Lord, paralleling Jacob's family who gave up their foreign gods.
Hosea mentions earrings linked to Baal worship, shedding light on why the earrings in Gen 35:4 were buried together with the foreign gods.
The connection shows a theological contrast between the burial of idols and the burial of the faithful Joseph in the same holy land.
An allusion to the same holy land at Shechem and the tradition of its purchase, linking the heritage of the patriarchs.
